messages.subject: Dynamic allocation array
parts:
Hello! 

I'm trying to implement a function in the functions block in STAN. However, I do not know if I can allocate dynamically a vector. To be more precise, let us say I want to build a function that returns an array of matrices whose length is variable (but known, denoted by T for each user i). 

functions {

  matrix[s,s] Q_mat[T[i]](int i,int s,vector[s*s-s] mu,matrix[k,s*s-s] beta,int T_in[n],int T[n]) {
  
    /*
    Calculation here...
    */
 
    return Q_mat;
  }

}

However, the result from parser is: 

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'model3D' with error message:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

ERROR at line 5
  3:    functions {
  4:    
  5:      matrix[s,s] Q_mat[T[i]](int i,int s,vector[s*s-s] mu,matrix[k,s*s-s] beta,int T_in[n],int T[n]) {
                ^
  6:

What am I doing wrong? 

Thank you very much in advance

User defined function declarations do not input (or check) the sizes of input or output. Write it like

functions {

  matrix[] Q_mat(int i,int s, vector mu, matrix beta, int[] T_in ,int[] T) {

/*
   Calculation here...
   */
    return Q_mat;
 }
}

Thank you so much, now my function is working. I still have a little issue, though:  

 matrix[] Q_mat(int i,int s,vector mu,matrix beta,int[] T_in,int[] T,matrix X,int k) {
  
    matrix<lower=0,upper=1>[s,s] Q_mat[T[i]]; 
    matrix<lower=0>[T[i],k] X_trunc; 

    X_trunc <- block(X, T_in[i]+1, 1, T[i], k);

    Q_mat[,1,1] <- 1 ./ (1 + exp(mu[1] + X_trunc * col(beta,1)) + exp(mu[2] + X_trunc * col(beta,2)));
    Q_mat[,1,2] <- exp(mu[1] + X_trunc * col(beta,1)) ./ (1 + exp(mu[1] + X_trunc * col(beta,1)) + exp(mu[2] + X_trunc * col(beta,2)));
    Q_mat[,1,3] <- exp(mu[2] + X_trunc * col(beta,2)) ./ (1 + exp(mu[1] + X_trunc * col(beta,1)) + exp(mu[2] + X_trunc * col(beta,2)));
    Q_mat[,2,1] <- exp(mu[3] + X_trunc * col(beta,3)) ./ (1 + exp(mu[3] + X_trunc * col(beta,3)) + exp(mu[4] + X_trunc * col(beta,4)));
    Q_mat[,2,2] <- 1 ./ (1 + exp(mu[3] + X_trunc * col(beta,3)) + exp(mu[4] + X_trunc * col(beta,4)));
    Q_mat[,2,3] <- exp(mu[4] + X_trunc * col(beta,4)) ./ (1 + exp(mu[3] + X_trunc * col(beta,3)) + exp(mu[4] + X_trunc * col(beta,4)));
    Q_mat[,3,1] <- exp(mu[5] + X_trunc * col(beta,5)) ./ (1 + exp(mu[5] + X_trunc * col(beta,5)) + exp(mu[6] + X_trunc * col(beta,6)));
    Q_mat[,3,2] <- exp(mu[6] + X_trunc * col(beta,6)) ./ (1 + exp(mu[5] + X_trunc * col(beta,5)) + exp(mu[6] + X_trunc * col(beta,6)));
    Q_mat[,3,3] <- 1 ./ (1 + exp(mu[5] + X_trunc * col(beta,5)) + exp(mu[6] + X_trunc * col(beta,6)));
 
    return Q_mat;
  }

What I am trying to do is to assign each element of the array of matrices. On the right hand size I have some vectors, on the left hand side I would like to get a vector corresponding to the element (i,j) for each one of the matrices, with an R-like syntax Q_mat[,i,j]. However, STAN outputs this error 

ERROR at line 12

 12:        Q_mat[,1,1] <- 1 ./ (1 + exp(mu[1] + X_trunc * col(beta,1)) + exp(mu[2] + X_trunc * col(beta,2)));
                  ^

Hi Giorgio,

We currently don't allow R / Matlab like slicing of arrays of matrices. This might be available at some point in the future, but for now, you'll have to do the assignment by hand.


Daniel
